principles.claim_en: Ibn Qudāma defines qiyās in the sharʿ as carrying a farʿ onto an aṣl in a ḥukm by a common factor (jāmiʿ), listing two further definitions as near-equivalent.
principles.excerpt_ar: حمل فرع على أصل في حكم بجامع بينهما

principles.claim_en: He rejects defining qiyās as ijtihād, since ijtihād is wider (it includes reasoning from ʿumūmāt and other proofs).
principles.excerpt_ar: وقيل: هو الاجتهاد وهو خطأ، فإن الاجتهاد قد يكون بالنظر في العمومات وسائر طرق الأدلة، وليس بقياس

principles.claim_en: Every qiyās requires four pillars: aṣl, farʿ, ʿilla, ḥukm; logical syllogism (two premises) is not properly called qiyās.
principles.excerpt_ar: ولا بد في كل قياس من أصل، وفرع، وعلة، وحكم

principles.claim_en: ʿIlla is defined as the manāṭ (anchor) of the ruling; named from the illness that changes the state of the patient.
principles.excerpt_ar: ونعني بالعلة: مناط الحكم. وسميت علة؛ لأنها غيرت حال المحل

principles.claim_en: Ijtihād regarding the ʿilla is of three kinds: taḥqīq, tanqīḥ and takhrīj al-manāṭ. Taḥqīq al-manāṭ: the general rule is agreed or textual and one verifies it in the particular (e.g. cow as the "like" for the wild ass; qibla direction); no dispute over its permissibility.
principles.excerpt_ar: ومعناه: أن تكون القاعدة الكلية متفقا عليها، أو منصوصا عليها، ويجتهد في تحقيقها في الفرع

principles.claim_en: Tanqīḥ al-manāṭ: the Lawgiver links a ruling to its cause with attached descriptions that have no role, which must be deleted so the ruling extends (the Bedouin who had intercourse in Ramaḍān); most deniers of qiyās accept it.
principles.excerpt_ar: وهو: أن يضيف الشارع الحكم إلى سببه، فيقترن به أوصاف لا مدخل لها في الإضافة، فيجب حذفها عن الاعتبار، ليتسع الحكم

principles.claim_en: Takhrīj al-manāṭ: the Lawgiver states a ruling without indicating its manāṭ and the mujtahid extracts it by reasoning (intoxication for wine, measurability for wheat-ribā); this is the disputed qiyās proper.
principles.excerpt_ar: فيستنبط المناط بالرأي والنظر

principles.claim_en: Some Ḥanbalīs hold that worship by qiyās is permissible rationally and legally, citing Aḥmad: "no one can dispense with qiyās"; the Ẓāhirīs and al-Naẓẓām deny it rationally and legally; a report from Aḥmad ("avoid mujmal and qiyās") is interpreted by al-Qāḍī as qiyās contradicting a text.
principles.excerpt_ar: وذهب أهل الظاهر والنظام إلى أنه لا يجوز التعبد به عقلا ولا شرعا
principles.hanbali_position: Aṣḥābunā: taʿabbud bi-l-qiyās is valid ʿaqlan and sharʿan (Aḥmad: lā yastaghnī aḥad ʿan al-qiyās); Aḥmad's apparent dispraise of qiyās is read by al-Qāḍī Abū Yaʿlā as qiyās that contradicts a naṣṣ.

principles.claim_en: The legal proof for qiyās is the consensus of the Companions on judging by ra'y in cases devoid of text (e.g. Abū Bakr's imamate, fighting zakāt-withholders).
principles.excerpt_ar: إجماع الصحابة -رضي الله عنهم- على الحكم بالرأي في الوقائع الخالية عن النص

principles.claim_en: Against al-Naẓẓām, who held that an explicitly stated (manṣūṣ) ʿilla extends by wording/generality rather than qiyās, Ibn Qudāma replies that "I forbade wine for its intoxicating strength" covers only wine by its wording.
principles.excerpt_ar: قال النظام: العلة المنصوص عليها توجب الإلحاق بطريق اللفظ والعموم، لا بطريق القياس

principles.claim_en: Qiyās can go wrong in five ways: the ruling is not caused; the true ʿilla is missed; part of the ʿilla is omitted; an extraneous description is added; or the ʿilla is wrongly believed present in the farʿ.
principles.excerpt_ar: ويتطرق الخطأ إلى القياس من خمسة أوجه

principles.claim_en: Extending the unstated to the stated is either certain or presumptive; the certain kind has two forms: the unstated is more entitled to the ruling (mafhūm, e.g. blind animal vs one-eyed) or equal to it (slave woman like slave in sirāya), the latter being "negation of the distinguishing factor".
principles.excerpt_ar: أحدهما: أن يكون المسكوت عنه أولى بالحكم من المنطوق، وهو المفهوم

principles.claim_en: The equal case relies on knowing that the difference has no effect; its criterion is that no uniting ʿilla need be cited («التعرض للعلة الجامعة»), only negation of an effective difference; whether this is called qiyās is disputed.
principles.excerpt_ar: وضابط هذا الجنس: أن لا يحتاج فيه إلى التعرض للعلة الجامعة، بل بنفي الفارق المؤثر

principles.claim_en: The proofs establishing the ʿilla reduce to text (naṣṣ), consensus (ijmāʿ) or extraction (istinbāṭ).
principles.excerpt_ar: وأدلة الشرع ترجع إلى "نص" أو "إجماع" أو "استنباط" فهذه ثلاثة أقسام

principles.claim_en: First textual mode: explicit (ṣarīḥ) — a word of causation (taʿlīl) appears (kay lā, li-kay lā, dhālika bi-annahum, min ajli dhālika).
principles.excerpt_ar: الأول- الصريح: وذلك أن يرد فيه لفظ التعليل

principles.claim_en: Second textual mode: tanbīh and īmāʾ, of six kinds, the first being mention of the ruling after a description joined by fāʾ; the sixth is ruling coupled with a suitable description.
principles.excerpt_ar: الضرب الثاني، التنبيه والإيماء إلى العلة

principles.claim_en: The ʿilla may be established by consensus, e.g. the effect of minority on guardianship, anger as cause of the ban on judging.
principles.excerpt_ar: القسم الثاني. ثبوت العلة بالإجماع

principles.claim_en: Istinbāṭ has three kinds; first is munāsaba: the description coupled with the ruling is suitable, i.e. establishing the ruling after it secures a maṣlaḥa.
principles.excerpt_ar: ومعناه: أن يكون في إثبات الحكم عقيبه مصلحة

principles.claim_en: The munāsib is threefold: muʾaththir (effect shown by text or ijmāʿ), mulāʾim (its genus affects the ruling's species), gharīb (genus in genus).
principles.excerpt_ar: فالمناسب ثلاثة أنواع: مؤثر، وملائم، وغريب

principles.claim_en: Some restricted qiyās to the muʾaththir only; Ibn Qudāma rejects this since the Companions did not require text/ijmāʿ for every ʿilla and preponderant ẓann suffices.
principles.excerpt_ar: وقد قصر قوم القياس على المؤثر

principles.claim_en: Sabr: Abū al-Khaṭṭāb says it is valid only where the umma agrees the aṣl is muʿallal, differs over the ʿilla, and all but one candidate is refuted; structure: the ruling is muʿallal, the ʿilla is X or Y, X is void (buṭlān: «وقد بطل أحدهما»), so Y.
principles.excerpt_ar: فنقول: الحكم معلل، ولا علة إلا كذا أو كذا، وقد بطل أحدهما فيتعين الآخر

principles.claim_en: The shurūṭ (sharṭ) of sabr include that the enumeration be exhaustive (by the opponent's agreement or by searching until unable to find another).
principles.excerpt_ar: الأمر الثاني: أن يكون سبره حاصرا لجميع ما يعلل به

principles.claim_en: Naqḍ alone does not suffice to void (ifsād: «في إفساد علة خصمه») the opponent's ʿilla in sabr, since the cancelled element may be a part or sharṭ of the ʿilla.
principles.excerpt_ar: ولا يكفيه في إفساد علة خصمه: النقض

principles.claim_en: Third mode of istinbāṭ: dawarān — the ruling exists with the description and ceases with its absence (prohibition with intoxicating strength in wine); it yields ẓann; some require it to be combined with sabr.
principles.excerpt_ar: النوع الثالث- في إثبات العلة: أن يوجد الحكم بوجودها، ويعدم بعدمها

principles.claim_en: "Testimony of the uṣūl" (e.g. horses: no zakāt in males alone so none in mixed herds) is supported by al-Qāḍī and some Shāfiʿīs and rejected by others.
principles.excerpt_ar: ذهب القاضي وبعض الشافعية إلى صحته

principles.claim_en: Invalid maslak: proving an ʿilla's ṣiḥḥa by its mere concomitance (iṭṭirād) is fāsid («ففاسد»)—absence of one defeater (naqḍ) is not proof of soundness.
principles.excerpt_ar: فأما الدلالة على صحة العلة باطرادها ففاسد

principles.claim_en: If the suitable description entails an equal or greater mafsada: some say munāsaba lapses; Ibn Qudāma says this is not correct because maṣlaḥa is a real thing not annulled by an opposing factor.
principles.excerpt_ar: متى لزم من الوصف المتضمن للمصلحة مفسدة مساوية للمصلحة، أو راجحة عليها

principles.claim_en: Qiyās al-shabah: al-Qāḍī Yaʿqūb defines it as a farʿ oscillating between a permitting and prohibiting aṣl and joined to the one it resembles more (the slave between the free man and the beast).
principles.excerpt_ar: هو أن يتردد الفرع بين أصلين: حاظر ومبيح، ويكون شبهه بأحدهما أكثر

principles.claim_en: Alternative definition: shabah unites aṣl and farʿ by a description suggestive (yuhim) of containing the wisdom—between the clearly suitable (qiyās al-ʿilla, «وهو صحيح») and the clearly irrelevant (ṭard, «باطل»).
principles.excerpt_ar: فالقسم الأول: قياس العلة، وهو صحيح

principles.claim_en: There are two reports from Aḥmad on qiyās al-shabah: ṣaḥīḥ («أنه صحيح»), and not ṣaḥīḥ (chosen by al-Qāḍī); al-Shāfiʿī has two corresponding views. Ibn Qudāma gives the argument for its authority (it yields preponderant ẓann).
principles.excerpt_ar: واختلفت الرواية عن أحمد -رحمه الله- في قياس الشبه: فروي: أنه صحيح
principles.hanbali_position: Two riwāyas from Aḥmad: shabah is ḥujja / is not ḥujja; al-Qāḍī Abū Yaʿlā chose invalidity; Ibn Qudāma argues for its being ḥujja (yuthīru ẓannan ghāliban).

principles.claim_en: Qiyās al-dalāla: joining farʿ and aṣl by an indicator of the ʿilla, whose sharing indicates sharing in the ʿilla and hence apparently in the ruling (compelling the virgin: married while silent so also while displeased).
principles.excerpt_ar: وهو: أن يجمع بين الفرع والأصل بدليل العلة

principles.claim_en: First sharṭ of the aṣl: it is established by text or agreement of both disputants; one cannot ground the aṣl itself by qiyās on another aṣl.
principles.excerpt_ar: أحدهما: أن يكون ثابتا بنص، أو اتفاق من الخصمين

principles.claim_en: Some Ḥanbalīs allow qiyās on what was itself established by qiyās (it becomes an aṣl); Ibn Qudāma suggests they meant when both disputants agree.
principles.excerpt_ar: وقال بعض أصحابنا: يجوز القياس على ما ثبت بالقياس
principles.hanbali_position: Dispute among the aṣḥāb: some allow qiyās on an aṣl established by qiyās; Ibn Qudāma restricts it to an aṣl agreed by both parties.

principles.claim_en: Some require the aṣl to be agreed on by the whole umma (to avoid al-qiyās al-murakkab); Ibn Qudāma rejects this on two grounds.
principles.excerpt_ar: وقال قوم: من شرطه: أن يكون متفقا عليه بين الأمة

principles.claim_en: A textual aṣl may be used even if disputed between the parties, provided the text does not itself cover the farʿ (otherwise the qiyās is a pointless detour).
principles.excerpt_ar: بشرط أن يكون النص غير متناول للفرع

principles.claim_en: Second sharṭ: the ruling of the aṣl must be rationally intelligible (maʿqūl al-maʿnā); prayer times and numbers of rakʿas cannot be extended.
principles.excerpt_ar: أن يكون الحكم معقول المعنى، إذ القياس إنما هو: تعدية الحكم من محل إلى محل بواسطة تعدي المقتضى

principles.claim_en: Shurūṭ (sharṭ) of the ḥukm: (1) the farʿ's ruling must equal the aṣl's (no extension with excess or deficiency, e.g. eclipse prayer rukūʿ argument rejected);
principles.excerpt_ar: أحدهما: أن يكون حكم الفرع مساويا لحكم الأصل

principles.claim_en: (2) the ruling must be sharʿī: rational rulings and uṣūl questions cannot be established by qiyās, as they are definitive; linguistic qiyās is disputed.
principles.excerpt_ar: الشرط الثاني: أن يكون الحكم شرعيا

principles.claim_en: Sharṭ of the farʿ: the ʿilla of the aṣl must be present in it; the precedence of the aṣl in time is required only for qiyās al-ʿilla, not qiyās al-dalāla; presence of the ʿilla in the farʿ need only be probable.
principles.excerpt_ar: والصحيح: أن ذلك يشترط لقياس العلة، ولا يشترط لقياس الدلالة

principles.claim_en: The legal ʿilla means a sign (ʿalāma); it may be a sharʿī ruling, an accidental or inherent description, an act, simple or compound, negative or positive, suitable or not.
principles.excerpt_ar: ومعنى العلة الشرعية: العلامة

principles.claim_en: Our companions say transitivity (taʿdiya) is a sharṭ of the ʿilla's ṣiḥḥa («من شرط صحة العلة: أن تكون متعدية»), so a restricted (qāṣira) ʿilla like thamaniyya for gold/silver is not ṣaḥīḥ (also Ḥanafī view); Abū al-Khaṭṭāb, with the Shāfiʿīs, allows the qāṣira.
principles.excerpt_ar: قال أصحابنا: من شرط صحة العلة: أن تكون متعدية
principles.hanbali_position: Intra-madhhab khilāf: aṣḥābunā require mutaʿaddiya; Abū al-Khaṭṭāb permits taʿlīl bi-l-ʿilla al-qāṣira.

principles.claim_en: On iṭṭirād: al-Barmakī reports two wajhs — it is a sharṭ of its ṣiḥḥa («شرطا لصحتها»; naqḍ voids an extracted ʿilla, or shows a texted one to be partial), supported by al-Qāḍī; or the ʿilla remains ḥujja elsewhere like a specified general term, chosen by Abū al-Khaṭṭāb (also Mālik, Ḥanafīs).
principles.excerpt_ar: حكى أبو حفص البرمكي في كون ذلك شرطا لصحتها وجهين
principles.hanbali_position: Two wajhs (al-Barmakī): naqḍ invalidates (al-Qāḍī) vs takhṣīṣ allowed (Abū al-Khaṭṭāb); a third view distinguishes manṣūṣa (not defeated) from mustanbaṭa (defeated), which Ibn Qudāma defends.

principles.claim_en: A third view distinguishes: naqḍ of an extracted ʿilla invalidates it («مبطلا لها»), but a text- or ijmāʿ-based ʿilla is not impaired by non-occurrence of the ruling (a missing sharṭ or present impediment).
principles.excerpt_ar: وفرق قوم بين العلة المنصوص عليها، وبين المستنبطة، وجعل نقض المستنبطة مبطلا لها

principles.claim_en: Four ways to escape naqḍ: deny the ʿilla in the case, deny the ruling, show the case is an exception against both principles, or show an impediment/missing sharṭ there.
principles.excerpt_ar: فإذا طريق الخروج عن عهدة النقض أربعة أمور

principles.claim_en: Three kinds of non-occurrence of ruling that do not count as naqḍ: (1) exceptions to the qiyās rule (ʿāqila, muṣarrāt, ʿarāyā) which specify (yukhaṣṣiṣ) the ʿilla rather than void it («ولا يفسد العلة»); (2) a competing ʿilla; (3) absence of the proper locus or sharṭ.
principles.excerpt_ar: فلا يوجب نقضا على القياس، ولا يفسد العلة، بل يخصصها بما وراء الاستثناء

principles.claim_en: An exception to qiyās that is rationally understood can serve as an aṣl (grapes on dates in ʿarāyā; other forbidden things in necessity); one not understood cannot (Abū Burda's goat, Khuzayma's testimony).
principles.excerpt_ar: فالأول: يصح أن يقاس عليه ما وجدت فيه العلة

principles.claim_en: Abū al-Khaṭṭāb: the ʿilla may be a negation of a quality, name or ruling according to aṣḥābunā; some Shāfiʿīs deny causation by non-existence; Ibn Qudāma permits it because legal causes are signs.
principles.excerpt_ar: قال أبو الخطاب: يجوز أن تكون العلة: نفي صفة، أو اسم، أو حكم، على قول أصحابنا
principles.hanbali_position: Aṣḥābunā (per Abū al-Khaṭṭāb) allow taʿlīl bi-l-ʿadam.

principles.claim_en: A ruling may be caused by two ʿillas, since legal causes are signs (touching and urinating together).
principles.excerpt_ar: يجوز تعليل الحكم بعلتين

principles.claim_en: Qiyās in causes (asbāb): some allow it (sodomy on zinā for stoning), others deny; Ibn Qudāma affirms it via tanqīḥ al-manāṭ and via the ḥikma (anger → hunger/thirst for judging).
principles.excerpt_ar: قال قوم: يجوز إجراء القياس في الأسباب
principles.hanbali_position: Ibn Qudāma (ولنا) affirms qiyās in asbāb.

principles.claim_en: Qiyās runs in kaffārāt and ḥudūd (also Shāfiʿī view), against the Ḥanafīs who argue measures are known only to God and ḥudūd are averted by doubt.
principles.excerpt_ar: ويجري القياس في الكفارات والحدود
principles.hanbali_position: Ḥanbalī (with Shāfiʿīs): qiyās applies in ḥudūd and kaffārāt; Ḥanafīs deny.

principles.claim_en: What is not known in its rationale (numbers of rakʿas etc.) is not subject to qiyās.
principles.excerpt_ar: فأما ما لا نعلمه: كأعداد الركعات ونحوه: فلا يجري القياس فيه

principles.claim_en: Original negation (nafy aṣlī) is not subject to qiyās al-ʿilla but can take qiyās al-dalāla; supervening negation takes both.
principles.excerpt_ar: فلا يجري فيه قياس العلة؛ لأنه لا موجب له قبل ورود السمع

principles.claim_en: Twelve questions can be directed at qiyās: istifsār, fasād al-iʿtibār, fasād al-waḍʿ, manʿ, taqsīm, muṭālaba, naqḍ, qawl bi-l-mūjab, qalb, ʿadam al-taʾthīr, muʿāraḍa, tarkīb.
principles.excerpt_ar: قال بعض أهل العلم: يتوجه على القياس اثنا عشر سؤالا

principles.claim_en: Istifsār is directed at an ambiguous term; the objector need only show two possible meanings.
principles.excerpt_ar: أما الاستفسار: فيتوجه على المجمل

principles.claim_en: Fasād al-iʿtibār: the objection that the qiyās contradicts a text and so is bāṭil («فيكون باطلا»)—the Companions did not resort to qiyās once they had a report.
principles.excerpt_ar: وهو أن يقول: هذا قياس يخالف نصا، فيكون باطلا

principles.claim_en: Fasād al-waḍʿ: showing that the ʿilla requires the opposite of the ruling attached to it (hiba-formula marriage example).
principles.excerpt_ar: وهو: أن يبين أن الحكم المعلق على العلة تقتضي العلة نقيضه

principles.claim_en: Manʿ has four loci: denial of the aṣl ruling, of the ʿilla's existence in the aṣl, of its causality, of its existence in the farʿ; the correct view: the mustadill is not cut off by denial of the aṣl ruling.
principles.excerpt_ar: وقد اختلف في انقطاع المستدل عند توجه منع الحكم في الأصل: والصحيح: أنه لا ينقطع

principles.claim_en: Taqsīm: has two shurūṭ (sharṭ)—the mustadill's term must divide into accepted and denied senses, and the division must be exhaustive.
principles.excerpt_ar: ويشترط لصحته شرطان. أحدهما: أن يكون ما ذكره المستدل منقسما إلى

principles.claim_en: Muṭālaba: demand that the mustadill prove that the jāmiʿ is the ʿilla; it is in effect the third manʿ.
principles.excerpt_ar: وهي: طلب المستدل بذكر ما يدل على أن ما جعله جامعا هو العلة

principles.claim_en: Naqḍ: showing the ʿilla without the ruling; Ibn Qudāma has preferred the view that naqḍ is a valid objection; it is fitter that the mustadill guard against naqḍ cases in his proof.
principles.excerpt_ar: ومعناه: إبداء العلة بدون الحكم
principles.hanbali_position: Ibn Qudāma: 'we preferred the view of whoever holds naqḍ valid' (rajjaḥnā qawl man qāla bi-ṣiḥḥat al-naqḍ).

principles.claim_en: Kasr—showing the ḥikma without the ruling—is not binding, since the ḥikma cannot be measured by opinion.
principles.excerpt_ar: وهو إبداء الحكمة بدون الحكم: فغير لازم

principles.claim_en: Adding a non-effective description (ṭardī) to the ʿilla to fend off naqḍ does not work (istijmār example); some disagreed.
principles.excerpt_ar: وإذا احترز عن النقض بذكر وصف في العلة لا أثر له في الحكم

principles.claim_en: Qalb: the objector derives from the mustadill's own proof a ruling contrary to his, keeping aṣl and description; two kinds (supporting the objector's school / refuting the opponent's); qalb is a kind of muʿāraḍa.
principles.excerpt_ar: ومعناه: أن يذكر لدليل المستدل حكما ينافي حكم المستدل، مع تبقية الأصل والوصف بحالهما

principles.claim_en: Muʿāraḍa is in the aṣl (better, needs no aṣl of its own) or in the farʿ (needs an aṣl and the objector becomes mustadill); the correct view is that it is accepted.
principles.excerpt_ar: وأحسنهما: المعارضة في الأصل؛ لأنه لا يحتاج إلى ذكر غير صلاحية ما يذكره، ولا يحتاج إلى أصل

principles.claim_en: Muʿāraḍa in the farʿ: citing in the farʿ what prevents the ruling, either a stronger proof (text/ijmāʿ: «بدليل آكد منه») or a description.
principles.excerpt_ar: وهو: أن يذكر في الفرع ما يمتنع معه ثبوت الحكم

principles.claim_en: ʿAdam al-taʾthīr: the proof contains something superfluous to establishing the aṣl ruling—because the ruling holds without it or because it is a ṭardī description.
principles.excerpt_ar: ومعناه: أن يذكر في الدليل ما يستغنى عنه في إثبات الحكم في الأصل

principles.claim_en: Tarkīb: qiyās compounded from the differing position of the opponent (female adult like a fifteen-year-old); views differ whether it is valid.
principles.excerpt_ar: وهو: القياس المركب من اختلاف مذهب الخصم

principles.claim_en: Al-qawl bi-l-mūjab: conceding what the mustadill made the consequence of his proof while the dispute remains; it is the last of the questions; whether the objector must show his basis is disputed.
principles.excerpt_ar: وحقيقته: تسليم ما جعله المستدل موجبا لدليله، مع بقاء الخلاف

principles.claim_en: Other objections include the deniers' "this is qiyās in religion" and the Ḥanafī "qiyās in ḥudūd and kaffārāt"; the ordering of objections is disputed but agreed to be better.
principles.excerpt_ar: وقد اختلف في وجوب ترتيب الأسئلة

principles.claim_en: Our companions say an ʿilla is preferred by what a report is preferred by (agreement with another proof, a Companion's view, etc.); preference by prohibitive vs permissive rulings is disputed.
principles.excerpt_ar: قال أصحابنا: ترجح العلة بما يرج به الخبر
principles.hanbali_position: Aṣḥābunā: ʿilla is preferred by the same factors as a khabar.

principles.claim_en: Al-Qāḍī prefers a sensible (ḥissī) ʿilla over a juridical one; Abū al-Khaṭṭāb inclines to the ḥukmī one.
principles.excerpt_ar: فاختار القاضي ترجيح الحسية
principles.hanbali_position: Khilāf: al-Qāḍī prefers ḥissiyya, Abū al-Khaṭṭāb ḥukmiyya.

principles.claim_en: Further preferences: ʿilla drawn from several uṣūl; muṭṭarida-munʿakisa over non-reversing; mutaʿaddiya over qāṣira (preferred); one whose aṣl is agreed upon.
principles.excerpt_ar: ورجح العلة المطردة المنعكسة على ما لا ينعكس

principles.claim_en: The muʾaththira ʿilla is preferred over the mulāʾima, the mulāʾima over the gharīb, and the munāsiba over the shabahiyya.
principles.excerpt_ar: وترجح العلة المؤثرة على الملائمة

principles.claim_en: Clear and hidden qiyās: some define jalī as qiyās al-ʿilla and khafī as qiyās al-shabah; others: jalī is where the meaning is evident (the angry judge).
principles.excerpt_ar: ففسره قوم: بأنه قياس العلة، والخفي: بقياس الشبه

principles.claim_en: Matn: qiyās is technically carrying a farʿ onto an aṣl in a ruling by a common factor; alternatives: establishing the like of a ruling outside its locus for a shared muqtaḍī («لمقتض مشترك»), or extending the text's ruling; defining it as ijtihād is wrong.
principles.excerpt_ar: وشرعا: حمل فرع على أصل في حكم بجامع بينهما، وقيل: إثبات مثل الحكم في غير محله لمقتض مشترك

principles.claim_en: Al-Ṭūfī: qiyās in language denotes equalisation generally; in the sharʿ it is a specific equalisation of aṣl and farʿ—a conventional (ʿurfī) reality and linguistic majāz.
principles.excerpt_ar: وهو في الشرع تسوية خاصة بين الأصل والفرع، فهو كتخصيص لفظ الدابة ببعض مسمياتها

principles.claim_en: Matn: pillars are aṣl, farʿ, ʿilla, ḥukm; aṣl is either the text (ribā ḥadīth) or its locus (the six commodities); the ʿilla is a farʿ in the aṣl (extracted from the ruling) and an aṣl in the farʿ.
principles.excerpt_ar: وأركانه: أصل، وفرع، وعلة، وحكم. فالأصل: قيل: النص، كحديث الربا، وقيل: محله كالأعيان الستة

principles.claim_en: Matn: taḥqīq al-manāṭ — showing that the requirement of an agreed or textual general rule, or the known ʿilla, exists in the farʿ (the "like" in game penalties, qibla, maintenance; the cat's ṭawwāf ʿilla applied to mice).
principles.excerpt_ar: ويسميان: تحقيق المناط

principles.claim_en: Matn: tanqīḥ al-manāṭ — attributing causality to some of the descriptions accompanying the ruling and discarding the rest (Bedouin, beating his chest, his wife, that Ramaḍān); most deniers of qiyās accept it.
principles.excerpt_ar: وقال به أكثر منكري القياس

principles.claim_en: Matn: takhrīj al-manāṭ is "the qiyās-based ijtihād"; our companions permitted worship by it rationally and legally, as did most jurists and theologians, against the Ẓāhiriyya and al-Naẓẓām; Aḥmad hinted at denial, interpreted as qiyās contrary to a text.
principles.excerpt_ar: وهو الاجتهاد القياسي، وأجاز أصحابنا التعبد به عقلا وشرعا، وبه قال عامة الفقهاء والمتكلمين خلافا للظاهرية والنظام
principles.hanbali_position: Aṣḥābunā: taʿabbud by qiyās permitted ʿaqlan and sharʿan; Aḥmad's apparent dispraise read as qiyās against a naṣṣ.

principles.claim_en: Al-Ṭūfī maps eight positions (rational/legal × permissible/obligatory/impossible/occurring); among those denying its actual occurrence: Dāwūd b. ʿAlī al-Iṣbahānī, al-Qāshānī and al-Nahrawānī.
principles.excerpt_ar: ومنعه داود بن علي الأصبهاني والقاشاني والنهرواني

principles.claim_en: Matn argument: qiyās involves warding off a presumed harm, which is rationally obligatory, so qiyās is rationally obligatory, and obligation entails permissibility.
principles.excerpt_ar: القياس يتضمن دفع ضرر مظنون، وهو واجب عقلا، فالقياس واجب عقلا

principles.claim_en: Matn reply to deniers who cite "We have neglected nothing in the Book": the meaning is laying down the paths of iʿtibār, of which qiyās is one; judging by qiyās is referral to God and the Messenger.
principles.excerpt_ar: والحكم بالقياس رد إلى الله والرسول، إذ عنهما تلقينا دليله

principles.claim_en: Matn: sharṭ of the aṣl—established by text (even if the parties dispute it) or agreed between the two, even if established by qiyās; not provable by qiyās on another aṣl.
principles.excerpt_ar: فشرط الأصل ثبوته بنص، وإن اختلفا فيه ; أو اتفاق منهما ولو ثبت بقياس

principles.claim_en: Matn: further shurūṭ (sharṭ)—the aṣl's proof must not cover the farʿ, and the aṣl ruling must be rationally intelligible.
principles.excerpt_ar: وأن لا يتناول دليل الأصل الفرع وإلا لاستغني عن القياس. وأن يكون معقول المعنى

principles.claim_en: Matn: the farʿ ruling must equal the aṣl ruling (else multiple ʿillas or one ʿilla with unequal effects); and it must be sharʿī, not rational or a doctrinal uṣūl matter.
principles.excerpt_ar: وشرط حكم الفرع مساواته لحكم الأصل

principles.claim_en: Matn: the farʿ must contain the aṣl's ʿilla (probable presence suffices); precedence of the aṣl is required for qiyās al-ʿilla, not qiyās al-dalāla.
principles.excerpt_ar: وشرط الفرع وجود علة الأصل فيه ظنا إذ هو كالقاطع في الشرعيات

principles.claim_en: Matn: the legal ʿilla is a sign and identifier; it must be transitive, so the qāṣira (thamaniyya) is disregarded—Ḥanafī view—against al-Shāfiʿī, Abū al-Khaṭṭāb and most theologians.
principles.excerpt_ar: أما العلة الشرعية فهي علامة ومعرف، ومن شرطها أن تكون متعدية فلا عبرة بالقاصرة
principles.hanbali_position: Matn reports aṣḥāb requiring mutaʿaddiya; Abū al-Khaṭṭāb dissents.

principles.claim_en: Matn: on iṭṭirād (constancy) of the ʿilla: al-Qāḍī and some Shāfiʿīs require it; Mālik, Ḥanafīs, Abū al-Khaṭṭāb do not, so after takhṣīṣ it remains ḥujja like a general term; other views: only with an impediment; or manṣūṣa but not mustanbaṭa.
principles.excerpt_ar: واشترطه القاضي وبعض الشافعية، خلافا لبعضهم، ولمالك، والحنفية، وأبي الخطاب، فتبقى بعد التخصيص حجة كالعموم
principles.hanbali_position: Al-Qāḍī: iṭṭirād is a sharṭ («واشترطه القاضي»; naqḍ invalidates: ibṭāl); Abū al-Khaṭṭāb: takhṣīṣ al-ʿilla allowed.

principles.claim_en: Al-Ṭūfī: the dispute arises from two conflicting presumptions—an ʿilla with a proof is retained (non-occurrence may be due to impediment) vs the ruling's absence presumes absence of its cause; the "with impediment" view thus has force (wine-drinking under duress example).
principles.excerpt_ar: قلت: قد تعارض هنا أصلان، فخرج الخلاف لملاحظتهما

principles.claim_en: Matn: the ʿilla may be negative (ʿadamī)—against some Shāfiʿīs—and a ruling may have two ʿillas (touch and urination for wuḍūʾ), because legal causes are signs.
principles.excerpt_ar: ويجوز أن تكون العلة أمرا عدميا

principles.claim_en: Matn: al-Naẓẓām held a textual ʿilla extends by wording, not qiyās; rejected.
principles.excerpt_ar: ثم قال النظام: العلة المنصوصة توجب الإلحاق لا قياسا بل لفظا وعموما

principles.claim_en: Matn: textual proof of the ʿilla is ṣarīḥ (kay lā, li-kay lā, min ajli, ḥadhar) or īmāʾ; "innahā rijs / laysat bi-najas" are ṣarīḥ according to Abū al-Khaṭṭāb but īmāʾ for others.
principles.excerpt_ar: فصريح أيضا عند أبي الخطاب
principles.hanbali_position: Abū al-Khaṭṭāb counts 'innahā …' as explicit causation.

principles.claim_en: Matn: the second textual mode is īmāʾ, first kind being the ruling following a description with fāʾ ("it is harm, so keep away").
principles.excerpt_ar: الثاني: الإيماء وهو أنواع: أحدها: ذكر الحكم عقيب الوصف بالفاء

principles.claim_en: Matn: establishing the ʿilla by ijmāʿ, e.g. minority for guardianship, the judge's preoccupied heart.
principles.excerpt_ar: القسم الثاني: إثباتها بالإجماع، كالصغر للولاية

principles.claim_en: Matn: munāsaba—a suitable description coupled with the ruling, where maṣlaḥa is expected to follow; need not originate the ḥikma; muʾaththir if its ʿayn or jins affects the ruling's ʿayn by text/ijmāʿ, mulāʾim if its jins affects the ʿayn, gharīb if jins in jins.
principles.excerpt_ar: أحدها: إثباتها بالمناسبة، وهي أن يقترن بالحكم وصف مناسب، وهو ما تتوقع المصلحة عقيبه

principles.claim_en: Matn: some restrict qiyās to the muʾaththir (others possibly taʿabbudī or due to an unknown description).
principles.excerpt_ar: وقصر قوم القياس على المؤثر

principles.claim_en: Matn: sabr—voiding (ibṭāl: «إبطال كل علة») every ʿilla proposed for a ruling agreed to be caused except one; the enumeration must be exhaustive; a description is not voided by naqḍ alone.
principles.excerpt_ar: النوع الثاني السبر: وهو إبطال كل علة علل بها الحكم المعلل إجماعا، إلا واحدة فتعين

principles.claim_en: Matn: dawarān—existence of the ruling with the description and absence with its absence; it yields ẓann of causality (ʿilliyya); al-Qāḍī and some Shāfiʿīs accept "testimony of the uṣūl".
principles.excerpt_ar: النوع الثالث الدوران: وهو وجود الحكم بوجود الوصف، وعدمه بعدمه وخالف قوم

principles.claim_en: Matn: iṭṭirād of an ʿilla does not prove its validity—freedom from naqḍ does not exclude another defeater; validity requires a positive proof.
principles.excerpt_ar: خاتمة اطراد العلة لا يفيد صحتها

principles.claim_en: Matn: qiyās al-shabah—two definitions; the shabahī description is between the suitable (qiyās al-ʿilla) and the ṭardī («طردي باطل»); two views each from Aḥmad and al-Shāfiʿī; "the more apparent: yes" (to the ṣiḥḥa of holding by it, «وفي صحة التمسك به»), as it yields ẓann—against al-Qāḍī"; resemblance is in ruling not reality (against Ibn ʿUlayya).
principles.excerpt_ar: والثالث: الشبه، وفي صحة التمسك به قولان لأحمد والشافعي - رضي الله عنهما -، والأظهر: نعم لإثارته الظن، خلافا للقاضي
principles.hanbali_position: Two riwāyas from Aḥmad; Mukhtaṣar (al-Ṭūfī) prefers validity of shabah, against al-Qāḍī.

principles.claim_en: Matn: qiyās al-dalāla joins aṣl and farʿ by an indicator of the ʿilla (silent virgin; the slave's marriage).
principles.excerpt_ar: قياس الدلالة: الجمع بين الأصل والفرع بدليل العلة

principles.claim_en: Matn: the ʿilla being a sign, it can be an accidental or inherent description, an act, a legal ruling, simple or compound, suitable or not, existential or non-existential, and not limited to seven components.
principles.excerpt_ar: ولا تنحصر أجزاؤها في سبعة أوصاف، خلافا لقوم

principles.claim_en: Matn: qiyās runs in asbāb, kaffārāt and ḥudūd (Shāfiʿīs agree), against the Ḥanafīs; proof: Companions' consensus on qiyās without distinction, e.g. the drunkard's ḥadd by analogy with the slanderer.
principles.excerpt_ar: ويجري القياس في الأسباب والكفارات والحدود، وهو قول الشافعية خلافا للحنفية
principles.hanbali_position: Ḥanbalī: qiyās in asbāb, ḥudūd, kaffārāt.

principles.claim_en: Sharḥ: qiyās in muqaddarāt, ḥudūd and kaffārāt (zakāt thresholds, prayer counts, arsh, ḥadd amounts) is the madhhab of Aḥmad, al-Shāfiʿī and most, against Abū Ḥanīfa; where the meaning is not understood, no qiyās.
principles.excerpt_ar: هو مذهب أحمد، والشافعي، وابن القصار والباجي من المالكية وأكثر الناس، خلافا لأبي حنيفة وأصحابه
principles.hanbali_position: Madhhab Aḥmad: qiyās in muqaddarāt where the maʿnā is understood.

principles.claim_en: Matn: original negation takes only qiyās al-dalāla (confirming istiṣḥāb); supervening negation takes both kinds.
principles.excerpt_ar: والنفي ضربان: أصلي: فيجري فيه قياس الدلالة

principles.claim_en: Matn: the objections are said to be twelve; first istifsār, directed at ambiguity; the objector need only show two possible meanings.
principles.excerpt_ar: الأسئلة الواردة على القياس قيل: اثنا عشر

principles.claim_en: Matn: fasād al-iʿtibār is the qiyās contradicting a text (Muʿādh's ḥadīth; the Companions only used qiyās absent a text); answered by denying the text or showing the qiyās deserves precedence.
principles.excerpt_ar: وهو مخالفة القياس نصا، كحديث معاذ

principles.claim_en: Matn: fasād al-waḍʿ—the ʿilla requires the opposite of what was attached to it (hiba-formula marriage).
principles.excerpt_ar: وهو اقتضاء العلة نقيض ما علق بها

principles.claim_en: Matn: manʿ—denial of the aṣl ruling (the mustadill is not cut off by it, per al-aṣaḥḥ, «على الأصح»), of the ʿilla in the aṣl, of its causality, of its presence in the farʿ.
principles.excerpt_ar: المنع، وهو منع حكم الأصل، ولا ينقطع به المستدل على الأصح

principles.claim_en: Matn: taqsīm—the objector enumerates the possible meanings of what the mustadill claims as the ʿilla and cancels them; must divide into denied and conceded senses and be exhaustive.
principles.excerpt_ar: وهو حصر المعترض مدارك ما ادعاه المستدل علة وإلغاء جميعها

principles.claim_en: Matn: muṭālaba—demanding the proof of causality (ʿilliyya); concedes the ruling and the description in aṣl and farʿ; it is the third of the denials.
principles.excerpt_ar: وهي طلب دليل علية الوصف من المستدل

principles.claim_en: Matn: naqḍ—the ʿilla without the ruling; whether it voids the ʿilla is disputed («وفي بطلان العلة به خلاف»); the mustadill should guard against naqḍ cases; may answer "I do not know the riwāya there".
principles.excerpt_ar: وهو إبداء العلة بدون الحكم، وفي بطلان العلة به خلاف

principles.claim_en: Matn: kasr (the ḥikma without the ruling) is not binding since ḥikmas are not measurable by opinion; adding a non-effective description to avoid naqḍ fails; adding a sharṭ in the ruling works per Abū al-Khaṭṭāb.
principles.excerpt_ar: والكسر: وهو إبداء الحكمة بدون الحكم، غير لازم
principles.hanbali_position: Abū al-Khaṭṭāb: naqḍ can be avoided by a condition placed in the ḥukm.

principles.claim_en: Matn: qalb—attaching the negation of the mustadill's ruling to his very ʿilla; either to support the objector's school or to refute the mustadill's.
principles.excerpt_ar: القلب، وهو تعليق نقيض حكم المستدل على علته بعينها

principles.claim_en: Matn: muʿāraḍa in the aṣl shows another cause for the ruling there (a muqtaḍī: «وجود مقتض للحكم فيه»); al-aṣaḥḥ («على الأصح») obliges the mustadill to exclude it in his proof.
principles.excerpt_ar: المعارضة، وهي إما في الأصل ببيان وجود مقتض للحكم فيه

principles.claim_en: Matn: ʿadam al-taʾthīr—mentioning what the proof does not need for the aṣl ruling, because it is ṭardī or the ruling holds without it.
principles.excerpt_ar: عدم التأثير، وهو ذكر ما يستغني عنه الدليل في ثبوت حكم الأصل

principles.claim_en: Matn: tarkīb—qiyās compounded from both madhhabs; validity disputed; "the first (validity) is better".
principles.excerpt_ar: ففي صحة التمسك به خلاف

principles.claim_en: Matn: al-qawl bi-l-mūjab—conceding the proof while denying the conclusion, or conceding its requirement while claiming the dispute remains; the last of the questions.
principles.excerpt_ar: القول بالموجب، وهو: تسليم الدليل مع منع المدلول

principles.claim_en: Matn: all objections reduce to manʿ or muʿāraḍa; some count 25; ordering them is agreed to be better, its obligatoriness is disputed.
principles.excerpt_ar: والأسئلة راجعة إلى منع، أو معارضة، وإلا لم يسمع

principles.claim_en: Matn: tarjīḥ qiyāsī is by aṣl, ʿilla or supporting indicator; an aṣl established by ijmāʿ beats one by text; qiyās on many uṣūl beats qiyās on one (against al-Juwaynī).
principles.excerpt_ar: فحكم الأصل الثابت بالإجماع، راجح على الثابت بالنص لعصمة الإجماع

principles.claim_en: Matn: by the ʿilla: consensual over others, manṣūṣa over mustanbaṭa, munāsiba over others, the one referred to an aṣl on which the Lawgiver himself drew analogy, muṭṭarida and munʿakisa ones.
principles.excerpt_ar: فتقدم العلة المجمع عليها على غيرها، والمنصوصة، على المستنبطة

principles.claim_en: Matn: technically qiyās is "returning a farʿ to an aṣl by a uniting ʿilla" (al-Qāḍī, Abū al-Khaṭṭāb, Ibn al-Bannāʾ); in sharʿ generally it is equalising a farʿ with an aṣl in a ruling (al-Ṭūfī: conventional reality, linguistic majāz).
principles.excerpt_ar: رد فرع إلى أصل بعلة جامعة
principles.hanbali_position: Definition attributed to al-Qāḍī Abū Yaʿlā, Abū al-Khaṭṭāb and Ibn al-Bannāʾ.

principles.claim_en: Matn: the definition does not intend qiyās al-dalāla—joining aṣl and farʿ by an indicator of the ʿilla (wine/nabīdh by the smell indicating intoxication).
principles.excerpt_ar: ولم يرد بالحد قياس الدلالة وهو: الجمع بين أصل وفرع بدليل العلة

principles.claim_en: Matn: nor qiyās al-ʿaks—establishing the contrary of a known ruling in another case because they differ in the ʿilla (fasting in iʿtikāf); shown to be ḥujja by Qurʾān (law kāna fīhimā ālihatun), sunna (sexual act as ṣadaqa) and Companions; whether it is called qiyās: three views, preferred: metaphorically.
principles.excerpt_ar: ولا قياس العكس، وهو: تحصيل نقيض حكم المعلوم في غيره، لافتراقهما في علة الحكم
principles.hanbali_position: Ibn Mufliḥ: qiyās al-ʿaks is ḥujja, stated by al-Qāḍī and other aṣḥāb.

principles.claim_en: Matn: its pillars are four: aṣl, farʿ, ʿilla, ḥukm; Ibn al-Najjār notes legal qiyās reduces to a logical two-premise syllogism.
principles.excerpt_ar: ثم اعلم أن القياس الشرعي راجع في الحقيقة إلى القياس العقلي المنطقي المؤلف من المقدمتين

principles.claim_en: Matn: the aṣl is the locus of the ruling compared to (jurists); others: the proof of the ruling, or the ruling itself—a verbal dispute (Ibn Qāḍī al-Jabal); Ibn ʿAqīl: the ruling and the ʿilla.
principles.excerpt_ar: فالأصل محل الحكم المشبه به

principles.claim_en: Matn shurūṭ (sharṭ) of ḥukm al-aṣl: it must be sharʿī (if a sharʿī ruling is sought), not abrogated, not covering the farʿ's ruling, and not deviating from the course of qiyās.
principles.excerpt_ar: وشرط حكم الأصل: كونه شرعيا إن استلحق شرعيا

principles.claim_en: Deviation from the norm of qiyās is of two kinds: not rationally understood (Khuzayma's testimony, number of rakʿas, zakāt thresholds, ḥadd and kaffāra amounts) or understood but without parallel (travel concessions, qasāma).
principles.excerpt_ar: أو لم يستثن "كعدد الركعات" وتقدير نصاب الزكاة ومقادير الحدود والكفارات

principles.claim_en: Matn: what is specified out of qiyās may serve as an aṣl and be compared to another; Abū Yaʿlā cites Aḥmad on vowing (nadhr) to slaughter oneself (he ransoms himself with a ram, «يفدي نفسه بكبش»: fidāʾ, by analogy with vowing one's son); Ibn Mufliḥ: view of aṣḥābunā and Shāfiʿīs.
principles.excerpt_ar: وما خص من القياس يجوز القياس عليه و" يجوز "قياسه على غيره
principles.hanbali_position: Aṣḥābunā: qiyās on what is excepted from qiyās is valid (Aḥmad's vow-of-self-slaughter case).

principles.claim_en: The aṣl need only be agreed between the two disputants (al-ṣaḥīḥ, «وهذا الصحيح الذي عليه الجمهور»); some require the umma's agreement; al-Muwaffaq rejected that due to the rarity of consensual rulings.
principles.excerpt_ar: وضعفه الموفق كغيره لندرة المجمع عليه

principles.claim_en: Matn: one may draw analogy on a general term that has been specified (sodomite and bestialist on the adulterer).
principles.excerpt_ar: ويقاس على عام خص، كلائط وآت بهيمة على زان

principles.claim_en: Matn: naqḍ, called takhṣīṣ al-ʿilla, is non-constancy—the ʿilla found without the ruling (fast without pre-dawn intention, contradicted by voluntary fasting).
principles.excerpt_ar: والنقض، ويسمى تخصيص العلة" هو "عدم اطرادها

principles.claim_en: Ten views on whether naqḍ impairs the ʿilla (qadḥ). First: it does not impair at all and the ʿilla is ḥujja in the rest, like a specified general term—al-Qāḍī and Abū al-Khaṭṭāb, attributed by al-Āmidī to most Ḥanbalīs; al-Qāḍī: the apparent view of Aḥmad.
principles.excerpt_ar: وهذا قول القاضي وأبي الخطاب. وحكاه الآمدي عن أكثر أصحابنا
principles.hanbali_position: Majority Ḥanbalī (al-Qāḍī, Abū al-Khaṭṭāb; 'ẓāhir kalām Aḥmad'): takhṣīṣ al-ʿilla allowed—naqḍ does not invalidate.

principles.claim_en: Second view: naqḍ impairs the ʿilla («يقدح»)—chosen among Ḥanbalīs by Ibn Ḥāmid and also by al-Qāḍī (two views), the Shāfiʿī position; al-Māturīdī: takhṣīṣ al-ʿilla is void.
principles.excerpt_ar: والقول الثاني: يقدح. اختاره من أصحابنا: ابن حامد وقاله القاضي أيضا
principles.hanbali_position: Ibn Ḥāmid (and al-Qāḍī in another statement): naqḍ invalidates.

principles.claim_en: Third view: naqḍ impairs (qadḥ) the extracted ʿilla unless due to an impediment or missing sharṭ, but not the textual one—the choice of al-Muwaffaq in the Rawḍa. Sixth view (al-Fakhr Ismāʿīl): not allowed in manṣūṣa or exceptions like muṣarrāt.
principles.excerpt_ar: وهذا اختيار الشيخ موفق الدين في الروضة
principles.hanbali_position: Ibn Qudāma: naqḍ invalidates mustanbaṭa (absent impediment), not manṣūṣa.

principles.claim_en: Matn: kasr is the ḥikma existing without the ruling (a disobedient traveller vs one with arduous work at home); al-naqḍ al-maksūr is the naqḍ of some of the descriptions; al-ṣaḥīḥ among aṣḥābunā and most is that neither voids the ʿilla («لا يبطلانها»), since the ʿilla is the totality of descriptions.
principles.excerpt_ar: الصحيح عند أصحابنا والأكثر: أن الكسر والنقض المكسور "لا يبطلانها
principles.hanbali_position: Aṣḥābunā: kasr and naqḍ maksūr do not void the ʿilla.

principles.claim_en: Matn: reversibility (ʿaks)—absence of the ruling with absence of the ʿilla—is a sharṭ.
principles.excerpt_ar: والعكس، وهو عدم الحكم لعدم العلة شرط

principles.claim_en: Sharṭ: an extracted ʿilla must not be opposed by a contrary description in the aṣl absent from the farʿ; and must not contradict a text or ijmāʿ.
principles.excerpt_ar: لأن النص والإجماع لا يقاومهما القياس، بل يكون إذا خالفهما باطلا

principles.claim_en: Matn: the ʿilla must exist wholly in the farʿ; if the ʿilla is definitive and the farʿ more fitting, it is qiyās al-awlā (hitting parents vs "uff").
principles.excerpt_ar: شرط فرع: أن توجد" العلة "فيه" أي في الفرع "بتمامها

principles.claim_en: Matn: definitive ʿilla but not a fortiori = qiyās al-musāwāt (nabīdh on wine); presumptive ʿilla = qiyās al-adwan (apple on wheat by ṭaʿm).
principles.excerpt_ar: و" يسمى قياس "المساواة

principles.claim_en: Matn: the ʿilla must have effect in its aṣl (aṣḥābunā, Ḥanafīs, Shāfiʿīs); the farʿ ruling must equal the aṣl ruling in ʿayn or jins.
principles.excerpt_ar: أن تؤثر" العلة "في أصلها المقيس عليه" عند أصحابنا والحنفية والشافعية
principles.hanbali_position: Aṣḥābunā require taʾthīr of the ʿilla in its aṣl; al-Ḥulwānī: effect in any aṣl suffices.

principles.claim_en: Matn: the farʿ must not have a concordant text on its ruling; precedence of the farʿ ruling: required by Ḥanafīs/al-Āmidī, but al-Muwaffaq, al-Majd and al-Ṭūfī require it only for qiyās al-ʿilla.
principles.excerpt_ar: وقال الموفق والمجد والطوفي: يشترط لقياس العلة، لا لقياس الدلالة

principles.claim_en: First maslak: ijmāʿ (placed first for its strength): the umma agrees that a ruling's (ḥukm's) ʿilla is X (the angry judge: why he may not judge; the full brother's priority).
principles.excerpt_ar: والمراد بثبوت العلة بالإجماع: أن تجمع الأمة على أن هذا الحكم علته كذا

principles.claim_en: Second maslak: the naṣṣ, of which the ṣarīḥ is what is coined to convey causation and admits nothing else (li-ʿillat, sabab, ajl, min ajli).
principles.excerpt_ar: ومنه" أي من النص ما هو "صريح" وهو ما وضع لإفادة التعليل، بحيث لا يحتمل غير العلة

principles.claim_en: Text divides into ṣarīḥ, ẓāhir and īmāʾ/tanbīh; īmāʾ is coupling a description to a ruling such that, were it not the ʿilla, the coupling would be odd.
principles.excerpt_ar: والإيماء: هو اقتران الوصف بحكم لو لم يكن الوصف

principles.claim_en: Third maslak: al-sabr wa-l-taqsīm—enumerating the descriptions in the aṣl, cancelling what is unfit so the remainder is the ʿilla; the debater may say "I searched and found no other".
principles.excerpt_ar: وهو: حصر الأوصاف" في الأصل المقيس عليه "وإبطال ما لا يصلح

principles.claim_en: Al-Qāḍī: causation is the norm (taʿlīl al-aṣl) and acting on ẓann in ʿilal is obligatory by consensus.
principles.excerpt_ar: ويجب العمل بالظن فيها" أي في علل الأحكام "إجماعا

principles.claim_en: Fourth maslak: munāsaba, also called ikhāla; extracting the ʿilla by it is called takhrīj al-manāṭ: determining the aṣl's ʿilla by showing suitability from the description itself; the munāsib is that after which maṣlaḥa follows.
principles.excerpt_ar: الرابع " من مسالك العلة "المناسبة، و" يقال "الإخالة

principles.claim_en: Fifth maslak: shabah (slave between free man and beast; madhy between urine and semen); resemblance is in ruling not reality per most aṣḥāb and Shāfiʿīs (against Ibn ʿUlayya).
principles.excerpt_ar: الخامس " من مسالك العلة "إثباتها بالشبه

principles.claim_en: Matn: shabah is not resorted to where qiyās al-ʿilla is possible (al-Bāqillānī: consensus); otherwise it is ḥujja for us and the Shāfiʿīs (Ibn ʿAqīl: dissent counts for nothing); not ḥujja per al-Qāḍī, Ḥanafīs, al-Bāqillānī, al-Shīrāzī.
principles.excerpt_ar: فإن عدم" إمكان قياس العلة "فحجة" أي فقياس الشبه حجة عندنا
principles.hanbali_position: Madhhab: shabah is ḥujja when qiyās al-ʿilla is unavailable; al-Qāḍī dissents (not ḥujja).

principles.claim_en: Sixth maslak: dawarān (al-Āmidī/Ibn al-Ḥājib: ṭard wa-ʿaks)—the ruling ordered on a description in existence and absence; it yields ẓann of the ʿilla per most aṣḥāb, Mālikīs and Shāfiʿīs.
principles.excerpt_ar: ويفيد" الدوران "العلة ظنا" عند الأكثر من أصحابنا

principles.claim_en: Ṭard: concomitance of ruling and description without any suitability; not a proof by itself according to the four imams (Ibn al-Samʿānī: maʿnā is taḥqīq, shabah taqrīb, ṭard taḥakkum).
principles.excerpt_ar: وليس" الطرد "دليلا وحده" عند الأئمة الأربعة وغيرهم

principles.claim_en: Definitions: manāṭ = what the ruling is tied to; tanqīḥ = refining it; takhrīj = extracting it; taḥqīq = establishing the ʿilla in its particular instances; no dispute where the ʿilla is known by text or ijmāʿ.
principles.excerpt_ar: وتحقيقه": أي تحقيق المناط "إثبات العلة في آحاد صورها

principles.claim_en: Matn: qiyās is jalī when the absence of difference is certain (slave woman like slave in sirāya) or its ʿilla is textual or consensual; otherwise khafī.
principles.excerpt_ar: ما قطع فيه بنفي الفارق

principles.claim_en: Matn: by its ʿilla qiyās is qiyās ʿilla (cause stated), qiyās dalāla (joined by a concomitant, effect or ruling of the ʿilla), or qiyās fī maʿnā al-aṣl.
principles.excerpt_ar: قياس علة، وقياس دلالة، وقياس في معنى الأصل

principles.claim_en: Matn: worship by qiyās is rationally permissible per the four imams (al-Qāḍī, Abū al-Khaṭṭāb, al-Qaffāl and Abū al-Ḥusayn even held it rationally obligatory); it occurred legally per most aṣḥāb; denied by Dāwūd, his son, al-Qāshānī, al-Nahrawānī and some aṣḥāb—a riwāya from Aḥmad, interpreted by al-Qāḍī and Ibn ʿAqīl as qiyās against a text, and by Ibn Rajab as for one who did not search the proof.
principles.excerpt_ar: ومنعه داود وابنه والقاشاني والنهرواني وبعض أصحابنا وجمع، وهو رواية عن أحمد
principles.hanbali_position: Riwāya from Aḥmad apparently denying qiyās; al-Qāḍī/Ibn ʿAqīl read it as qiyās opposing naṣṣ; Ibn Rajab: most aṣḥāb record no khilāf from Aḥmad on acting by qiyās.

principles.claim_en: Matn: qiyās is ḥujja per most aṣḥāb; al-Qāḍī cites Aḥmad "no one can dispense with qiyās" and al-Shāfiʿī's "a necessity" which pleased Aḥmad; Ibn Ḥāmid reported from some aṣḥāb that it is not ḥujja.
principles.excerpt_ar: وقد احتج القاضي وغيره على العمل بالقياس بقول أحمد رحمه الله: لا يستغني أحد عن القياس

principles.claim_en: Abū Ḥanīfa and his followers deny qiyās in ḥadd, kaffāra, substitutes, rukhaṣ and fixed amounts; "for us" the general proof of qiyās and the Companion's "when he is drunk he raves…".
principles.excerpt_ar: ومنعه أبو حنيفة وأصحابه في حد وكفارة وبدل ورخص ومقدر
principles.hanbali_position: Ḥanbalī: qiyās runs in ḥudūd, kaffārāt, abdāl, rukhaṣ, muqaddarāt.

principles.claim_en: Some deny qiyās in sabab, sharṭ and impediment («في سبب وشرط ومانع»; zinā as sabab of ḥadd not extended to sodomy), as did al-Āmidī and Ibn al-Ḥājib; al-Āmidī reports most Shāfiʿīs allow it.
principles.excerpt_ar: ومنعه جمع في سبب وشرط ومانع

principles.claim_en: Matn: stating the ʿilla of the aṣl suffices for worship by qiyās per aṣḥābunā and most; Abū al-Khaṭṭāb, al-Muwaffaq and most Shāfiʿīs: only if worship by qiyās is established; Ibn Taymiyya: the first is "the qiyās of our madhhab".
principles.excerpt_ar: والنص على علة حكم الأصل يكفي في التعبد" عند أصحابنا والأكثر
principles.hanbali_position: Aṣḥābunā: a textual ʿilla suffices; Abū al-Khaṭṭāb and al-Muwaffaq require an established taʿabbud bi-l-qiyās.

principles.claim_en: Ibn Taymiyya, followed by Ibn al-Qayyim, held that nothing in the sharīʿa contradicts qiyās or lacks an understandable rationale.
principles.excerpt_ar: وقد ذكر الشيخ تقي الدين -وتبعه ابن القيم- أنه ليس في الشريعة ما يخالف القياس وما لا يعقل معناه

principles.claim_en: Knowing qiyās is farḍ kifāya, becoming individually obligatory for a sole mujtahid facing an urgent case; qiyās is "dīn".
principles.excerpt_ar: ومعرفته" أي معرفة القياس "فرض كفاية

principles.claim_en: Matn: the objections reduce to manʿ of premises or muʿāraḍa in the ruling; Ibn al-Ḥājib, Ibn Mufliḥ and most count 25 (some 12); istifsār heads them.
principles.excerpt_ar: القوادح ترجع إلى المنع في المقدمات، أو المعارضات في الحكم

principles.claim_en: Matn: fasād al-iʿtibār—the qiyās contradicting a text or ijmāʿ.
principles.excerpt_ar: الثاني: من القوادح "فساد الاعتبار

principles.claim_en: Matn: fasād al-waḍʿ is more specific than fasād al-iʿtibār: the qiyās is not in a form fit to yield the ruling (its ʿilla suits the contrary or contradictory ruling).
principles.excerpt_ar: الثالث: من القوادح "فساد الوضع

principles.claim_en: Matn: ʿadam al-taʾthīr—claim that the description has no suitability; it is not raised against qiyās al-dalāla (Ibn Taymiyya, Ibn ʿAqīl) nor against a negating qiyās; four sub-types.
principles.excerpt_ar: و "لا يرد" هذا "على قياس الدلالة" قاله الشيخ تقي الدين وابن عقيل

principles.claim_en: Matn: the mustadill should guard his proof against naqḍ; guarding by an effective-less description is not allowed; Abū al-Khaṭṭāb: guarding by deleting the ruling is not ṣaḥīḥ («بحذف الحكم لم يصح»).
principles.excerpt_ar: ويجب أن يحترز المستدل في دليله عن النقض

principles.claim_en: Matn: kasr ranks fourteenth; it is "like naqḍ" (Ibn Mufliḥ: naqḍ of the meaning).
principles.excerpt_ar: قال ابن مفلح: الكسر: نقض المعنى. والكلام فيه كالنقض

principles.claim_en: Matn: muʿāraḍa in the aṣl by another independent meaning; muʿāraḍa in the farʿ by what requires the contrary ruling—accepted per aṣḥābunā and most, so as not to undermine the object of debate.
principles.excerpt_ar: المعارضة في الفرع بما يقتضي نقيض حكم المستدل
principles.hanbali_position: Aṣḥābunā: muʿāraḍa in the farʿ is accepted.

principles.claim_en: Matn: tarkīb raised against al-qiyās al-murakkab; holding by it is "the sounder" view (al-aṣaḥḥ, «وهو الأصح») since it reduces to a dispute about the aṣl.
principles.excerpt_ar: وهو الأصح؛ لأن حاصله منازعة في الأصل

principles.claim_en: Matn: farq (21st) — the objector shows a meaning distinguishing aṣl from farʿ; it reduces to muʿāraḍa in the aṣl or farʿ and is accepted; the one objecting needs a proof and aṣl as with the jamʿ.
principles.excerpt_ar: وهو إبداء المعترض معنى يحصل به الفرق بين الأصل والفرع حتى لا يلحق به في حكمه

principles.claim_en: Matn: ikhtilāf al-ḍābiṭ (22nd)—the controlling factor differs between aṣl and farʿ (coercion vs false testimony to killing).
principles.excerpt_ar: اختلاف الضابط في الأصل والفرع

principles.claim_en: Matn: difference between the farʿ ruling and the aṣl ruling is an objection, answered by showing the ruling is identical (validity of sale and of marriage).
principles.excerpt_ar: مخالفة حكم الفرع لحكم الأصل

principles.claim_en: Matn: qalb (24th)—attaching the contrary of the ruling, or its concomitant, to the mustadill's ʿilla in relation to the aṣl; it is a kind of muʿāraḍa; also qalb al-dalīl.
principles.excerpt_ar: وهو "تعليق نقيض الحكم أو لازمه

principles.claim_en: Matn: al-qawl bi-l-mūjab—conceding what the proof requires while the dispute remains; Qurʾānic witness: "to God belongs might, and to His Messenger…".
principles.excerpt_ar: تسليم مقتضى الدليل مع بقاء النزاع

principles.claim_en: Matn: a qiyās is preferred if its ʿilla, or the proof of it, is definitive or of predominant probability.
principles.excerpt_ar: و" يرجح أحد القياسين على الآخر "بقطع علته

principles.claim_en: Matn: an ʿilla established by sabr beats one by munāsaba (sabr excludes an opposing factor), which beats shabah.
principles.excerpt_ar: و" يرجح أحد القياسين ب "سبر، فمناسبة

principles.claim_en: Ibn al-Qayyim: the sound qiyās (al-qiyās al-ṣaḥīḥ) is the "balance" (mīzān) revealed with the Book; the word qiyās is divisible into true and false, which is why the Qurʾān neither praises nor blames it; the false is e.g. likening ribā to sale.
principles.excerpt_ar: والقياس الصحيح هو الميزان؛ فالأولى تسميته بالاسم الذي سماه الله به

principles.claim_en: He explains that the salaf both blamed qiyās and used it: both are true (referring to the fāsid and the ṣaḥīḥ).
principles.excerpt_ar: ولهذا تجد في كلام السلف ذم القياس وأنه ليس من الدين، وتجد في كلامهم استعماله والاستدلال به، وهذا حق وهذا حق

principles.claim_en: Ibn al-Qayyim: the qiyāses used in reasoning are three—ʿilla, dalāla, shabah—all occurring in the Qurʾān (Jesus/Adam as qiyās al-ʿilla).
principles.excerpt_ar: والأقيسة المستعملة في الاستدلال ثلاثة: قياس علة، وقياس دلالة، وقياس شبه، وقد وردت كلها في القرآن

principles.claim_en: Qiyās al-dalāla is joining aṣl and farʿ by the indicator of the ʿilla and its concomitant (Qurʾānic resurrection arguments).
principles.excerpt_ar: وأما قياس الدلالة فهو الجمع بين الأصل والفرع بدليل العلة وملزومها

principles.claim_en: Ibn al-Qayyim: God reports qiyās al-shabah only from the people of falsehood (Joseph's brothers; ribā like sale by formal resemblance); it is refuted as devoid of an effective ʿilla.
principles.excerpt_ar: وأما قياس الشبه فلم يحكه الله سبحانه إلا عن المبطلين
principles.hanbali_position: Ibn al-Qayyim rejects shabah devoid of an effective cause, against the riwāya/Mukhtaṣar view that shabah is ḥujja.

principles.claim_en: In the deniers' presentation he cites Aḥmad (riwāya of Aḥmad b. al-Ḥusayn): qiyās is valid only when the thing is like the other in all its states; resembling in one and differing in another is an error—held by most Ḥanafīs, Mālikīs and Ḥanbalīs.
principles.excerpt_ar: القياس أن يقاس الشيء على الشيء إذا كان مثله في كل أحواله، فأما إذا أشبهه في حال وخالفه في حال فأردت أن تقيس عليه فهذا خطأ
principles.hanbali_position: Aḥmad's text (riwāya of Aḥmad b. al-Ḥusayn) against shabah-type analogy.

principles.claim_en: Reporting the disagreements of qiyāsīs: most extend qiyās to ʿibādāt, languages, ḥudūd and asbāb; some exclude ḥudūd and kaffārāt, others asbāb as well; all divide it into awlā, mithl and adnā.
principles.excerpt_ar: وكل هؤلاء قسموه إلى ثلاثة أقسام: قياس أولى، وقياس مثل، وقياس أدنى

principles.claim_en: Aḥmad's fifth principle: absent a text, a Companion's view, or a mursal/weak report, he resorts to qiyās out of necessity, citing al-Shāfiʿī: "one resorts to it only in necessity".
principles.excerpt_ar: عدل إلى الأصل الخامس - وهو القياس - فاستعمله للضرورة
principles.hanbali_position: Aḥmad uses qiyās only li-l-ḍarūra, after naṣṣ, fatwā of Companions, mursal/ḍaʿīf ḥadīth.

principles.claim_en: Neither ṣaḥīḥ texts nor sound qiyāses contradict each other; sound qiyās never contradicts sound text.
principles.excerpt_ar: فلا يناقض القياس الصحيح النص الصحيح أبدا

principles.claim_en: His middle position: the texts encompass all rulings; sound qiyās (al-qiyās al-ṣaḥīḥ) is true and conforms to the texts—"the Book and the Balance"—and one resorts to qiyās when a text's indication is hidden or has not reached the scholar.
principles.excerpt_ar: والقياس الصحيح حق مطابق للنصوص، فهما دليلان: الكتاب والميزان

principles.claim_en: The qiyāsīs' five errors include believing many rulings are against the mīzān/qiyās, considering ʿilal the Lawgiver did not consider and disregarding ones he did («اعتبارهم عللا وأوصافا لم يعلم اعتبار الشارع لها»), and contradicting themselves.
principles.excerpt_ar: الرابع: اعتبارهم عللا وأوصافا لم يعلم اعتبار الشارع لها وإلغاؤهم عللا وأوصافا اعتبرها الشارع

principles.claim_en: Ibn Taymiyya's answer (reported by Ibn al-Qayyim): "qiyās" is an ambiguous word covering ṣaḥīḥ and fāsid; the sound is joining like cases (ṭard) and separating unlike (ʿaks)—justice.
principles.excerpt_ar: والصحيح هو الذي وردت به الشريعة، وهو الجمع بين المتماثلين والفرق بين المختلفين، فالأول قياس الطرد، والثاني قياس العكس

principles.claim_en: Sound qiyās (al-qiyās al-ṣaḥīḥ): the ʿilla of the aṣl present in the farʿ without an impeding factor, or negation of any effective difference (ilghāʾ al-fāriq); the sharīʿa never contradicts it; where a text seems contrary, the qiyās is known to be unsound.
principles.excerpt_ar: وحيث علمنا أن النص ورد بخلاف قياس علمنا قطعا أنه قياس فاسد

principles.claim_en: Ibn al-Qayyim: if the farʿ has a distinguishing feature, rulings resting on it contradict only unsound qiyās; equal cases with different rulings never occur; equating cases that differ in what requires/prevents the ruling is the fāsid qiyās (qiyās maʿa al-fāriq).
principles.excerpt_ar: وأما التسوية بينهما في الحكم مع افتراقهما فيما يقتضي الحكم أو يمنعه فهذا هو القياس الفاسد

principles.claim_en: Unsound qiyās is the root of all evil: Iblīs was first to use it; Jahmiyya, Qadariyya, Rāfiḍa erred through it.
principles.excerpt_ar: فأصل شر الدنيا والآخرة جميعه من هذا القياس الفاسد

principles.claim_en: Ibn al-Qayyim: takhṣīṣ al-ʿilla is not impossible for want of a sharṭ or presence of an impediment; whether these are parts of the ʿilla is a verbal dispute (complete vs requiring cause).
principles.excerpt_ar: وبالجملة فلا يمتنع تخصيص العلة لفوات شرط أو لقيام مانع
principles.hanbali_position: Ibn al-Qayyim: takhṣīṣ for shart/māniʿ allowed; dispute verbal.

principles.claim_en: Ibn Taymiyya: qiyās al-tamthīl and qiyās al-shumūl are equal; certainty or probability depends on the content; the middle term of shumūl is what jurists call ʿilla, manāṭ, jāmiʿ.
principles.excerpt_ar: وأن قياس التمثيل وقياس الشمول سواء وإنما يختلف اليقين والظن بحسب المواد

principles.claim_en: Ibn Taymiyya: demanding proof of the effect of the description on the ruling (muṭālaba bi-taʾthīr al-waṣf) is the greatest objection against qiyās; its answer establishes the major premise via naṣṣ, ijmāʿ, sabr, munāsaba or dawarān.
principles.excerpt_ar: وهذا السؤال أعظم سؤال يرد على القياس

principles.claim_en: Ibn Taymiyya: qiyās al-shabah, if accepted, does not fall outside ʿilla or dalāla; if the jāmiʿ is neither the ʿilla nor entails it, sharing it does not entail sharing the ruling.
principles.excerpt_ar: وأما قياس الشبة فإذا قيل به لم يخرج عن أحدهما

principles.claim_en: Ibn Taymiyya: the validity of qiyās can be known by negation of the difference between aṣl and farʿ even without knowing the ʿilla or its proof.
principles.excerpt_ar: وقد يعلم صحة القياس بانتفاء الفارق بين الأصل والفرع وإن لم يعلم عين العلة ولا دليلها

principles.claim_en: Ibn Taymiyya: sound qiyās (al-qiyās al-ṣaḥīḥ) is part of the justice God revealed; a legal qiyās whose shurūṭ (sharṭ) are observed never contradicts a text; nothing in the sharīʿa is against sound qiyās, only against unsound.
principles.excerpt_ar: وليس في الشريعة شيء على خلاف القياس الصحيح بل على خلاف القياس الفاسد

principles.claim_en: Ibn Taymiyya: iʿtibār with punished nations includes qiyās al-ʿaks—establishing in the farʿ the opposite of the aṣl's ruling.
principles.excerpt_ar: وهذا قياس العكس وهو المقصود من الاعتبار بالمعذبين

principles.claim_en: Al-Nūrāniyya: those who held the ḥadīth on planting in another's land "against qiyās" did so from a qiyās they formed; what the sunna brought is the sound qiyās (al-qiyās al-ṣaḥīḥ) indicated by fiṭra.
principles.excerpt_ar: وما جاءت به السنة هو القياس الصحيح الذي تدل عليه الفطرة

principles.claim_en: Al-Shinqīṭī notes that in the first type of taḥqīq al-manāṭ "manāṭ" is not the technical ʿilla but the general text being applied to its instances.
principles.excerpt_ar: والمناطُ هنا ليس بمعناه الاصطلاحي

principles.claim_en: Al-Shinqīṭī: most uṣūlīs hold ghalabat al-ashbāh falls within shabah (against al-ʿAḍud).
principles.excerpt_ar: وأجمع جمهور الأصوليين على أنَّ غلبةَ الأشباهِ لا يخرجُ عن الشبه

principles.claim_en: Al-Shinqīṭī criticises Ibn Qudāma: his example for the second definition of shabah (wiping the head) is really the first (ghalabat al-ashbāh).
principles.excerpt_ar: الذي يظهرُ لي في كلام المؤلفِ -رحمه اللَّه- في هذا المسلكِ أنَّه لا يخلو مِنْ بعضِ نظرٍ

principles.claim_en: Al-Shinqīṭī: the question whether iṭṭirād is a sharṭ is the same as whether naqḍ impairs the ʿilla or specifies it.
principles.excerpt_ar: هو بعينه مبحثُ النقضِ هل هو قادحٌ في العلةِ أو مخصصٌ لعمومها

principles.claim_en: Al-Shinqīṭī lists views (most: takhṣīṣ, not qadḥ; Mālik: takhṣīṣ in mustanbaṭa, qadḥ in manṣūṣa) and prefers the reverse—a text-based ʿilla is not impaired (qadḥ) by naqḍ.
principles.excerpt_ar: وقال قومٌ بالعكس، وعزاهُ إمامُ الحرمين في البرهانِ للأكثر، وهو أوجه عندي مما قبله

principles.claim_en: Al-Shinqīṭī disputes Ibn Qudāma's claim that kasr is not binding: it is like naqḍ, so it impairs where naqḍ does.
principles.excerpt_ar: فالظاهرُ أنَّ الكسر كالنقض، فعلى أنَّ النقضَ قادحٌ فالكسرُ كذلك

principles.claim_en: Al-Shinqīṭī: the domains in which qiyās is disputed are seven (ḥudūd, kaffārāt, taqādīr, rukhaṣ, asbāb, shurūṭ, mawāniʿ); Ibn Qudāma chose its validity in ḥudūd and kaffārāt.
principles.excerpt_ar: اعلمْ أنَّ المسائل التي اختلف في جريان القياس فيها سبعٌ

principles.claim_en: Al-Shinqīṭī: the qawādiḥ originate in jadal; uṣūlīs include them as complements of the proof; some count 25 or 28.
principles.excerpt_ar: وأصلُ هذا المبحثِ من فنِّ الجدل، وإنَّما يذكره الأصوليون لأنَّه من مكملات الدليل

principles.claim_en: Al-Shinqīṭī (appendix): Ibn Ḥazm allows no ijtihād at all—no ruling except by text of Book or Sunna.
principles.excerpt_ar: فابن حزم يقول لا يجوز اجتهاد كائناً ما كان ولا يجوز أن يتكلم في حكم إلا بنص من كتاب أو سنة

principles.claim_en: Al-Shinqīṭī: even Dāwūd al-Ẓāhirī did not deny the qiyās al-Shāfiʿī calls "qiyās fī maʿnā al-aṣl".
principles.excerpt_ar: كان لا ينكر القياس المعروف الذي يسميه الشافعي القياس في معنى

principles.claim_en: Al-Shinqīṭī: the first to make an unsound qiyās rejecting God's texts was Iblīs.
principles.excerpt_ar: وأول من قاس قياساً فاسداً ورد فيه نصوص الله وأوامره ونواهيه هو إبليس اللعين

principles.claim_en: Ādāb: qiyās al-tamthīl (the jurists' qiyās) does not really differ from the logical syllogism of the first figure.
principles.excerpt_ar: لا فرق بينه وبين القياس المنطقي في الحقيقة

principles.claim_en: Ādāb: naqḍ in uṣūl is the ʿilla-description found while its ruling is absent; narrower than in munāẓara.
principles.excerpt_ar: وضابط النقض في اصطلاح الأصوليين هو وجود الوصف الذي هو العلةُ مع تخلف حكم العلة عنها

principles.claim_en: Ādāb: exceptions like ʿarāyā are by consensus not naqḍ but specification of the ʿilla's ruling.
principles.excerpt_ar: فالجواب أن هذا النوعَ ليس نقضًا للعلة بإجماع العلماء، وإنما هو تخصيص لحكمها

principles.claim_en: Ādāb: kasr is showing a defect in part of the ʿilla: ruling without ḥikma, ḥikma without ruling, or a defect (khalal) in part of a compound ʿilla.
principles.excerpt_ar: هو أن يبيّن المعترض خللًا في بعض أجزاء العلة

principles.claim_en: Ādāb: muʿāraḍa ʿalā sabīl al-qalb in munāẓara is the uṣūlī qalb: the objector proves the contrary of the mustadill's ruling by his very proof.
principles.excerpt_ar: أن يُثبت المعترض نقيض حكم المستدل بعين دليل المستدل، فيقلب دليله عليه لا له

principles.claim_en: Ādāb: fasād al-iʿtibār—the mustadill's proof contradicts a text or ijmāʿ (muṣarrāt qiyās vs the ṣāʿ of dates).
principles.excerpt_ar: فمخالفته للنص كقياس لبن المصراة على غيره من المِثْليات في وجوب رد المِثْل؛ فإنه فاسد الاعتبار

principles.claim_en: Ādāb: fasād al-waḍʿ—the proof is not in a form fit to yield the ruling (deriving leniency from strictness, etc.).
principles.excerpt_ar: وضابطه أن يكون الدليل على غير الهيئة الصالحة لأخذ الحكم منه

principles.claim_en: Ādāb: taqsīm is an objection to the proof according to the majority; some deny it.
principles.excerpt_ar: وهو قادح عند الجمهور في الدليل، ومنع قوم القدح به

principles.claim_en: Ādāb: ʿadam al-taʾthīr applies only to qiyās al-ʿilla with a disputed extracted ʿilla—not to shabah, ṭard, or textual/consensual ʿillas.
principles.excerpt_ar: يُشترط في القدح به أن يكون القياسُ قياسَ علة، فلا يُقدح به في قياس الشبه

principles.claim_en: Ādāb: muṭālaba and tarkīb are omitted as falling under manʿ.
principles.excerpt_ar: المسمى في الأصول بالمطالبة والقادحَ المسمى بالتركيب تركنا ذكرهما لأنهما داخلان في أقسام المنع

principles.claim_en: Ādāb: al-qawl bi-l-mūjab—the objector concedes the proof while the dispute remains (Ibn Ubayy's "the mightier will expel the meaner").
principles.excerpt_ar: وضابطه تسليم المعترض دليل الخصم مع بقاء النزاع

principles.claim_en: Ādāb: objection that the ruling does not lead to the maṣlaḥa for which it was legislated (permanent prohibition of in-laws).
principles.excerpt_ar: وضابطه الاعتراض بان المصلحة التي شُرع من أجلها الحكم لم يفض إليها الحكم

principles.claim_en: Ādāb: all qawādiḥ reduce to manʿ and muʿāraḍa; some say all reduce to manʿ.
principles.excerpt_ar: وقد قدمنا لك أن جميع القوادح راجعة إلى المنع والمعارضة

principles.claim_en: Ādāb: objection that the description is not well-defined (hardship for shortening prayer).
principles.excerpt_ar: وهو القادح المعروف في الأصول بكون الوصف غيرَ منضبط

principles.claim_en: Ibn ʿUthaymīn: qiyās is equating a farʿ with an aṣl in a ruling for a uniting ʿilla; its four pillars are farʿ, aṣl, ḥukm, ʿilla.
principles.excerpt_ar: واصطلاحاً: تسوية فرع بأصل في حكم لعلَّة جامعة بينهما

principles.claim_en: Ibn ʿUthaymīn cites al-Muzanī: jurists from the Companions on agreed that the like of truth is truth and used analogies in all rulings.
principles.excerpt_ar: أجمعوا على أن نظير الحق حق ونظير الباطل باطل

principles.claim_en: Ibn ʿUthaymīn, sharṭ 1: the qiyās must not clash with a stronger proof («دليلاً أقوى منه») (text, ijmāʿ, Companion's view if ḥujja)—else fāsid al-iʿtibār.
principles.excerpt_ar: أن لا يصادم دليلاً أقوى منه

principles.claim_en: Ibn ʿUthaymīn, sharṭ 2: the aṣl ruling must be established by text or ijmāʿ; one established by qiyās cannot be an aṣl.
principles.excerpt_ar: أن يكون حكم الأصل ثابتاً بنص أو إجماع، فإن كان ثابتاً بقياس لم يصح القياس عليه
principles.hanbali_position: Contrast with "some aṣḥāb" in Rawḍa who allow qiyās on a qiyās-established aṣl.

principles.claim_en: Ibn ʿUthaymīn, sharṭ 3: the aṣl ruling must have a known ʿilla; a purely taʿabbudī ruling (camel meat and wuḍūʾ) cannot be extended.
principles.excerpt_ar: فإن كان حكم الأصل تعبديًّا محضاً لم يصح القياس عليه

principles.claim_en: Ibn ʿUthaymīn, sharṭ 4: the ʿilla must contain a suitable meaning recognised by the sharʿ; a ṭardī description (black) cannot be a cause.
principles.excerpt_ar: أن تكون العلة مشتملة على معنى مناسب للحكم يعلم من قواعد الشرع اعتباره

principles.claim_en: Ibn ʿUthaymīn, sharṭ 5: the ʿilla must exist in the farʿ as in the aṣl.
principles.excerpt_ar: أن تكون العلة موجودة في الفرع كوجودها في الأصل

principles.claim_en: Ibn ʿUthaymīn: jalī is qiyās whose ʿilla is textual/consensual or with certain negation of difference; khafī is by istinbāṭ without such certainty.
principles.excerpt_ar: فالجلي: ما ثبتت علته بنص، أو إجماع، أو كان مقطوعاً فيه بنفي الفارق بين الأصل والفرع

principles.claim_en: Ibn ʿUthaymīn: qiyās al-shabah is weak (ḍaʿīf: «وهذا القسم من القياس ضعيف»), as there is no suitable ʿilla between farʿ and aṣl.
principles.excerpt_ar: وهذا القسم من القياس ضعيف إذ ليس بينه وبين الأصل علة مناسبة

principles.claim_en: Ibn ʿUthaymīn: qiyās al-ʿaks is establishing the contrary of the aṣl's ruling for the farʿ due to the contrary of its ʿilla.
principles.excerpt_ar: وهو: إثبات نقيض حكم الأصل للفرع لوجود نقيض علة حكم الأصل فيه

principles.claim_en: Ibn ʿUthaymīn: among qiyāses the jalī is preferred over the khafī.
principles.excerpt_ar: ويقدم من القياس: الجلي على الخفي

principles.claim_en: Al-Saʿdī (from Ibn Taymiyya): qiyās is blameworthy (lacking equality in manāṭ, or opposed by a text) or ṣaḥīḥ (aṣl and farʿ equal in manāṭ, unopposed by stronger proof: «ما هو أرجح منه»).
principles.excerpt_ar: وهو الذي يستوي فيه الأصل والفرع في مناط الحكم؛ ولم يعارضه ما هو أرجح منه

principles.claim_en: Al-Saʿdī (extract): sound qiyās (al-qiyās al-ṣaḥīḥ)—the aṣl's ʿilla present in the farʿ without opposing factor; the sharīʿa never contradicts it.
principles.excerpt_ar: القياس نوعان: صحيح وفاسدء فالصحيح أن تكون العلّة التى علق بها

principles.claim_en: Al-Saʿdī (extract): nothing in the sharīʿa contradicts qiyās; where it seems to, either the qiyās is unsound or the ruling is not established by text.
principles.excerpt_ar: ليس في الشريعة ما يخالف القياس. وما ظن فيه مخالفته للقياس، فأحد

principles.claim_en: Al-Saʿdī (extract on Aḥmad's uṣūl): failing all else he took qiyās out of necessity.
principles.excerpt_ar: أخذ بالقياس عند الضرورة
